title: Pairwise or Pointwise? Evaluating Feedback Protocols for Bias in LLM-Based Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: Modifying base responses to inject stylistic distractor features (confident/authoritative phrasing, increased verbosity/lexical complexity, or overly agreeable/flattering tone) while maintaining the original factual content or instruction-following quality, and then measuring how frequently LLM evaluators inappropriately favor the modified responses under pairwise versus absolute scoring protocols.

Examining cyclic preferences in LLM evaluations (e.g., A is preferred over B, B over C, but A is not preferred over C) by varying the order in which alternatives are presented in datasets like Ultrafeedback.

Testing whether the relative preference between two options reverses when a third, unrelated alternative is introduced or swapped within a choice set, violating the independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA).
